title: Extension by zero on the localizing categories
statement:
Work in the standing scheme setting of [sk-def-sfb-dc-setting]: fix a prime $\ell$ and a field $k$ of characteristic $p>0$ with $p\ne\ell$, and let $j\colon U\hookrightarrow X$ be an open immersion of separated finite-type $k$-schemes. Let $\Lambda$ be an admissible coefficient ring of [sk-def-localizing-closure]: a finite commutative ring killed by a power of $\ell$, or one of $\mathbf Z_\ell,\mathcal O_E,\mathbf Q_\ell,E,\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$, where $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ is finite inside a fixed algebraic closure and $\mathcal O_E$ is its valuation ring. Regard these as condensed rings with their indicated topologies. Use the ordinary unbounded module-object derived categories $D(\Mod_{\Lambda_T})$, where $\Lambda_T=p_T^*\Lambda$, and the bounded constructible finite-Tor subcategories $\Dctf(T,\Lambda)$ of [sk-def-sfb-constructible], for $T=U,X$.
Then extension by zero $j_!=D(j_!)$ maps $\Dctf(U,\Lambda)$ into $\Dctf(X,\Lambda)$, preserves all small direct sums on the ambient derived categories, and restricts to an exact, sum-preserving functor
$$
\Loc(\Dctf(U,\Lambda))\longrightarrow\Loc(\Dctf(X,\Lambda)).
$$
The localizing closures and their direct sums are taken in the ordinary ambient derived categories as in [sk-def-localizing-closure].

proof.text: Put $E=j_!$, $R=j^*$ and $J=D(E)$. [sk-def-sfb-module-lower-shriek] gives exactness and the adjunction. [lem-sf-exact-functor-derived-triangulated] makes $J$ triangulated; [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-bounded-below] gives $H^q(JK)\simeq E H^q(K)$ and preservation of every cohomological interval.

[det-def-localizing-closure-existence] supplies ambient sums and localizing closures. Termwise sums and [lem-weil-pbc-left-adjoint-preserves-colimits] for $E\dashv R$ give preservation by $J$: the degreewise comparisons form a chain isomorphism respecting coprojections. [lem-sf-full-subcategory-universe-coproduct-lift] supplies the ULift reindexing and inherited sums for both closures.

For $K\in\Dctf(U,\Lambda)$, use [sk-def-sfb-constructible] and the witness conversion of [lem-sf-constant-model-stratification-transport] on $U$. Apply [lem-sf-open-extension-zero-constant-model-constructible] to $H^q(K)$ with those witnesses. Apply the transport assertion to $EH^q(K)\simeq H^q(JK)$ from step 1. It gives the same finite scalar models on the extended strata and bounded constructibility of $JK$.

The two counits [def-sfb-upper-star-tensor-counit, def-sfb-derived-pullback-tensor-left-counit], [lem-sfb-derived-pullback-tensor-left-derived] and [lem-sfb-derived-pullback-tensor-comparison-iso] give $m$, with $\mu=m^{-1}$ by [lem-sfb-derived-pullback-strong-monoidal]. Transport via [def-sfb-left-derived-exact] and the canonical coefficient identification of [def-sfb-condensed-pullback-tensor-comparison]. Its unique localization equation is the same counit equation defining $m$, so the transported $m$ is $t^D$. Thus [def-sfb-open-closed-internal-hom-comparisons] defines precisely the mate of $\eta_K\otimes1$ followed by $\mu$. [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence](1) gives quasi-compactness of $j$ ($U$ qc, $X$ separated). Choose the reduced closed complement supplied in step 3. [lem-sfb-condensed-support-projection-formula] makes this mate $q_{K,L}:J(K\otimes^LLj^*L)\to JK\otimes^LL$ invertible.

proof.text: Use $P=Lj^*$ and its exact comparison [def-sfb-left-derived-exact]. Step 4 is precisely the projection hypothesis of [lem-sf-exact-adjoint-derived-tor-tests]. Its derived isomorphism identifies $JK\otimes^LN[0]$ with $J(K\otimes^L(j^*N)[0])$ for every module $N$ on $X$ and preserves the Tor interval from [sk-def-sfb-constructible]. Together with step 3 this proves $JK\in\Dctf(X,\Lambda)$.

By [sk-def-localizing-closure], target generators belong to their closure. Steps 1, 2 and 5 meet [det-proper-image-localizing-principle], which gives the object map into the target closure via its inverse-image intersection criterion. Apply [lem-sf-full-subcategory-universe-coproduct-lift] to the canonical lift: the inclusions create and preserve the smaller sums and the target inclusion reflects them. Its exactness and sum preservation follow.
